text: 12. A public confrontation in 1770 resulted in the deaths of five civilians at the hands of British regulars, an event that was immediately seized upon by Paul Revere and other patriots for propaganda purposes. While the loss of life was tragic, the label applied to the event suggested a slaughter of hundreds, a narrative choice designed to galvanize a revolution against the Crown. This "bloodbath" branding worked so well that the minor skirmish is still taught in history books under this hyperbolic title. What is the two-word name of this event?
